reranked.text:
DataFlow Systems Inc. alleges that Aurora's real-time data reconciliation engine
infringes U.S. Patent Nos. 9,847,221 and 10,112,905, both directed to methods
for incremental reconciliation of distributed record sets.

The four Aurora patents most closely related to the accused functionality are
U.S. Patent Nos. 10,445,882, 10,662,013, 11,004,776 and 11,238,450 — all naming
Dr. James Wu as first inventor.

Procedural posture as of March 15, 2024:
  - Aurora's motion to dismiss was denied in part on January 8, 2024.
  - Claim construction (Markman) hearing is scheduled for August 2024.
  - No trial date has been set. Counsel estimates trial no earlier than Q3 2025.

Exposure assessment by outside counsel (Wilson Sonsini):
  - Probable exposure range: $3.5 million to $8.0 million.
  - Counsel assesses the probability of an injunction as low, on the basis that
    DataFlow does not practise the asserted patents and would face difficulty
    demonstrating irreparable harm.
  - A licensing settlement in the range of $4 million to $6 million is
    considered the most likely outcome.

Financial statement treatment: the Company has NOT recorded a loss accrual, on
the basis that no loss is both probable and reasonably estimable within the
meaning of ASC 450. The range is disclosed but not accrued. Buyer's accounting
advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

Legal fees of $2.8 million were incurred in FY2023 in connection with this
matter and are treated as a non-recurring add-back in the quality of earnings
report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

The Company deleveraged materially during FY2023, driven by $52.1 million of
operating cash flow and a $25.0 million voluntary paydown of the revolver in
Q4 FY2023.

SECTION 3: NOTES TO NORMALIZATION ADJUSTMENTS
Note 1 - Restructuring Charges ($4.5M, FY2023)
    Severance and facility exit costs associated with the closure of the Austin
    development center in Q3 FY2023. 32 employees were affected. Management
    represents this program is complete and no further charges are expected.
    We consider this adjustment appropriate and non-recurring.

Note 2 - Non-recurring Legal Fees ($2.8M, FY2023)
    External counsel fees relating to the DataFlow Systems patent litigation
    (Case No. 2023-CV-04821). We note that this matter remains unresolved and
    that future periods may incur comparable fees. Buyer should treat this
    add-back with caution: it is non-recurring only if the litigation concludes.
    We have flagged this as a QUALIFIED ADJUSTMENT.

Note 3 - SOC 2 Remediation ($1.6M, FY2023)
    One-time external consulting and tooling spend to remediate control gaps
    identified in the FY2022 SOC 2 Type II examination. The FY2023 examination
    was issued with no exceptions. Adjustment accepted.

Note 4 - Founder Compensation Above Market ($1.9M, both years)
    CEO Elena Marsh and CTO Dr. James Wu receive aggregate cash compensation
    approximately $1.9 million above the 75th percentile of the peer benchmark
    set. Post-closing employment terms are addressed in the retention agreements
    described in the employment agreement schedule. Adjustment accepted.

Note 5 - Capitalized Software Adjustment (($3.2M), FY2023)
    The Company capitalizes internally developed software over a 3-year life.
    Peer practice in this segment is predominantly to expense. We have reduced
    EBITDA by the amount capitalized in each period to present a comparable
    figure. This is a DOWNWARD adjustment and reduces Adjusted EBITDA.

Note 6 - Deferred Revenue Haircut Reversal (($1.4M), FY2023)
    Purchase accounting will require a fair value haircut to acquired deferred
    revenue, estimated at $1.4 million. This reduces post-closing recognized
    revenue and is presented here so the Buyer models the correct run-rate.

SECTION 1: SCOPE AND BASIS OF PRESENTATION
This report presents a quality of earnings analysis of Aurora Technologies Inc.
(the "Company") for the fiscal years ended December 31, 2022 and December 31,
2023. Our procedures included analysis of revenue recognition policies, review
of accrual completeness, examination of non-recurring items, and normalization
of reported EBITDA.

This is not an audit. The Company's statutory financial statements were audited
by Deloitte & Touche LLP, which issued an unqualified opinion for both periods.

DataFlow Systems Inc. alleges that Aurora's real-time data reconciliation engine
infringes U.S. Patent Nos. 9,847,221 and 10,112,905, both directed to methods
for incremental reconciliation of distributed record sets.

The four Aurora patents most closely related to the accused functionality are
U.S. Patent Nos. 10,445,882, 10,662,013, 11,004,776 and 11,238,450 — all naming
Dr. James Wu as first inventor.

Procedural posture as of March 15, 2024:
  - Aurora's motion to dismiss was denied in part on January 8, 2024.
  - Claim construction (Markman) hearing is scheduled for August 2024.
  - No trial date has been set. Counsel estimates trial no earlier than Q3 2025.

Exposure assessment by outside counsel (Wilson Sonsini):
  - Probable exposure range: $3.5 million to $8.0 million.
  - Counsel assesses the probability of an injunction as low, on the basis that
    DataFlow does not practise the asserted patents and would face difficulty
    demonstrating irreparable harm.
  - A licensing settlement in the range of $4 million to $6 million is
    considered the most likely outcome.

Financial statement treatment: the Company has NOT recorded a loss accrual, on
the basis that no loss is both probable and reasonably estimable within the
meaning of ASC 450. The range is disclosed but not accrued. Buyer's accounting
advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

Legal fees of $2.8 million were incurred in FY2023 in connection with this
matter and are treated as a non-recurring add-back in the quality of earnings
report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

The Company deleveraged materially during FY2023, driven by $52.1 million of
operating cash flow and a $25.0 million voluntary paydown of the revolver in
Q4 FY2023.

SECTION 3: NOTES TO NORMALIZATION ADJUSTMENTS
Note 1 - Restructuring Charges ($4.5M, FY2023)
    Severance and facility exit costs associated with the closure of the Austin
    development center in Q3 FY2023. 32 employees were affected. Management
    represents this program is complete and no further charges are expected.
    We consider this adjustment appropriate and non-recurring.

Note 2 - Non-recurring Legal Fees ($2.8M, FY2023)
    External counsel fees relating to the DataFlow Systems patent litigation
    (Case No. 2023-CV-04821). We note that this matter remains unresolved and
    that future periods may incur comparable fees. Buyer should treat this
    add-back with caution: it is non-recurring only if the litigation concludes.
    We have flagged this as a QUALIFIED ADJUSTMENT.

Note 3 - SOC 2 Remediation ($1.6M, FY2023)
    One-time external consulting and tooling spend to remediate control gaps
    identified in the FY2022 SOC 2 Type II examination. The FY2023 examination
    was issued with no exceptions. Adjustment accepted.

Note 4 - Founder Compensation Above Market ($1.9M, both years)
    CEO Elena Marsh and CTO Dr. James Wu receive aggregate cash compensation
    approximately $1.9 million above the 75th percentile of the peer benchmark
    set. Post-closing employment terms are addressed in the retention agreements
    described in the employment agreement schedule. Adjustment accepted.

Note 5 - Capitalized Software Adjustment (($3.2M), FY2023)
    The Company capitalizes internally developed software over a 3-year life.
    Peer practice in this segment is predominantly to expense. We have reduced
    EBITDA by the amount capitalized in each period to present a comparable
    figure. This is a DOWNWARD adjustment and reduces Adjusted EBITDA.

Note 6 - Deferred Revenue Haircut Reversal (($1.4M), FY2023)
    Purchase accounting will require a fair value haircut to acquired deferred
    revenue, estimated at $1.4 million. This reduces post-closing recognized
    revenue and is presented here so the Buyer models the correct run-rate.

SECTION 4: CHANGE OF CONTROL AND THE TRANSACTION
Section 8.1(k) of the Credit Agreement defines an Event of Default to include
any transaction in which any person or group acquires beneficial ownership of
more than 35% of the voting equity of the Company.

The Vertex Capital Partners merger constitutes a change of control within this
definition. On the occurrence of such an Event of Default:

  - All commitments terminate automatically;
  - All outstanding principal, accrued interest and fees become immediately due
    and payable without further notice or demand.

Consequence for the transaction: the full $85 million drawn balance must be
repaid at closing. There is no prepayment penalty, but accrued interest and a
breakage indemnity for any SOFR period terminated mid-period will be payable.
Estimated breakage cost: less than $50,000.

The Company has NOT sought a consent or waiver from the lending syndicate.
Buyer's financing plan assumes the facility is repaid and replaced. The merger
agreement requires delivery of a customary payoff letter and lien releases at
closing as a condition to Buyer's obligation to close.

From the date of this Agreement until the earlier of the Effective Time or
termination of this Agreement, the Company shall not, and shall cause its
representatives not to, directly or indirectly: (a) solicit, initiate, or
knowingly facilitate any Acquisition Proposal; (b) enter into any agreement
regarding an Acquisition Proposal; or (c) provide non-public information to
any third party in connection with an Acquisition Proposal.

third party making an unsolicited Acquisition Proposal that the Board determines
in good faith (after consultation with outside counsel and financial advisors)
constitutes or could reasonably be expected to lead to a Superior Proposal.

are:

customer consents, notwithstanding that two material customer contracts

rights. Buyer therefore bears the risk of those consents not being obtained.

Counsel draws attention to this allocation: the customer consent risk sits with
the Buyer post-closing rather than operating as a condition, and is addressed,
if at all, through the indemnification provisions in Article VIII.

Section 8.1(k) of the Credit Agreement defines an Event of Default to include
any transaction in which any person or group acquires beneficial ownership of
more than 35% of the voting equity of the Company.

The Vertex Capital Partners merger constitutes a change of control within this
definition. On the occurrence of such an Event of Default:

  - All commitments terminate automatically;
  - All outstanding principal, accrued interest and fees become immediately due

breakage indemnity for any SOFR period terminated mid-period will be payable.

Section 8.1(k) of the Credit Agreement defines an Event of Default to include
any transaction in which any person or group acquires beneficial ownership of
more than 35% of the voting equity of the Company.

The Vertex Capital Partners merger constitutes a change of control within this
definition. On the occurrence of such an Event of Default:

  - All commitments terminate automatically;
  - All outstanding principal, accrued interest and fees become immediately due
    and payable without further notice or demand.

repaid at closing. There is no prepayment penalty, but accrued interest and a
breakage indemnity for any SOFR period terminated mid-period will be payable.

The Company has NOT sought a consent or waiver from the lending syndicate.

agreement requires delivery of a customary payoff letter and lien releases at
closing as a condition to Buyer's obligation to close.

reranked.text:
DataFlow Systems Inc. alleges that Aurora's real-time data reconciliation engine
infringes U.S. Patent Nos. 9,847,221 and 10,112,905, both directed to methods
for incremental reconciliation of distributed record sets.

The four Aurora patents most closely related to the accused functionality are
U.S. Patent Nos. 10,445,882, 10,662,013, 11,004,776 and 11,238,450 — all naming
Dr. James Wu as first inventor.

Procedural posture as of March 15, 2024:
  - Aurora's motion to dismiss was denied in part on January 8, 2024.
  - Claim construction (Markman) hearing is scheduled for August 2024.
  - No trial date has been set. Counsel estimates trial no earlier than Q3 2025.

Exposure assessment by outside counsel (Wilson Sonsini):
  - Probable exposure range: $3.5 million to $8.0 million.
  - Counsel assesses the probability of an injunction as low, on the basis that
    DataFlow does not practise the asserted patents and would face difficulty
    demonstrating irreparable harm.
  - A licensing settlement in the range of $4 million to $6 million is
    considered the most likely outcome.

Financial statement treatment: the Company has NOT recorded a loss accrual, on
the basis that no loss is both probable and reasonably estimable within the
meaning of ASC 450. The range is disclosed but not accrued. Buyer's accounting
advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

Legal fees of $2.8 million were incurred in FY2023 in connection with this
matter and are treated as a non-recurring add-back in the quality of earnings
report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

SECTION 3: MOST FAVORED NATION AND PRICING PROVISIONS
Northstar Financial Group holds a most favored nation ("MFN") pricing clause
entitling it to the lowest per-seat rate offered to any customer of comparable
volume. Management represents the MFN has not been triggered. Buyer diligence
identified one FY2023 arrangement (Continental Retail Group) priced 4% below the
Northstar rate at a lower volume tier; counsel has advised that the volume tiers
are not comparable and the MFN is therefore not triggered. This position has not
been tested with the customer.

Pacific Data Systems holds a price protection clause capping annual increases at
3% through the contract term ending June 30, 2025.

    add-back with caution: it is non-recurring only if the litigation concludes.

    identified in the FY2022 SOC 2 Type II examination. The FY2023 examination
    was issued with no exceptions. Adjustment accepted.

    approximately $1.9 million above the 75th percentile of the peer benchmark
    set. Post-closing employment terms are addressed in the retention agreements
    described in the employment agreement schedule. Adjustment accepted.

    EBITDA by the amount capitalized in each period to present a comparable
    figure. This is a DOWNWARD adjustment and reduces Adjusted EBITDA.

ARTICLE VIII — INDEMNIFICATION
Section 8.1 — Survival of Representations
The representations and warranties of the Company shall survive the Closing
for a period of eighteen (18) months, except that Fundamental Representations

DataFlow Systems Inc. alleges that Aurora's real-time data reconciliation engine
infringes U.S. Patent Nos. 9,847,221 and 10,112,905, both directed to methods
for incremental reconciliation of distributed record sets.

The four Aurora patents most closely related to the accused functionality are
U.S. Patent Nos. 10,445,882, 10,662,013, 11,004,776 and 11,238,450 — all naming
Dr. James Wu as first inventor.

Procedural posture as of March 15, 2024:
  - Aurora's motion to dismiss was denied in part on January 8, 2024.
  - Claim construction (Markman) hearing is scheduled for August 2024.
  - No trial date has been set. Counsel estimates trial no earlier than Q3 2025.

Exposure assessment by outside counsel (Wilson Sonsini):
  - Probable exposure range: $3.5 million to $8.0 million.
  - Counsel assesses the probability of an injunction as low, on the basis that
    DataFlow does not practise the asserted patents and would face difficulty
    demonstrating irreparable harm.
  - A licensing settlement in the range of $4 million to $6 million is
    considered the most likely outcome.

Financial statement treatment: the Company has NOT recorded a loss accrual, on
the basis that no loss is both probable and reasonably estimable within the
meaning of ASC 450. The range is disclosed but not accrued. Buyer's accounting
advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

Legal fees of $2.8 million were incurred in FY2023 in connection with this
matter and are treated as a non-recurring add-back in the quality of earnings
report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

Section 3.5 — Financial Statements
The Company has delivered to Buyer (a) the audited consolidated financial
statements for FY2022 and FY2023, (b) the unaudited quarterly financial
statements for Q1 2024 ended March 31, 2024. Such financial statements:
(i) were prepared in accordance with GAAP applied on a consistent basis,
(ii) fairly present in all material respects the consolidated financial
position and results of operations of the Company for the periods covered,
and (iii) are consistent with the books and records of the Company.

Section 8.2 — Indemnification Cap
The aggregate liability of the Company's stockholders for indemnification
claims under this Article VIII shall not exceed $69.6 million (representing
10% of the aggregate Merger Consideration) (the "General Cap"). For
Fundamental Representations, the cap shall be $174.0 million (25% of the
aggregate Merger Consideration).

Section 8.3 — Deductible
The Company's stockholders shall not be liable for indemnification claims
until the aggregate amount of Losses exceeds $3.48 million (representing
0.5% of the aggregate Merger Consideration) (the "Deductible"), after which
the Company's stockholders shall be liable for all Losses from the first dollar.

DataFlow Systems Inc. alleges that Aurora's real-time data reconciliation engine
infringes U.S. Patent Nos. 9,847,221 and 10,112,905, both directed to methods
for incremental reconciliation of distributed record sets.

The four Aurora patents most closely related to the accused functionality are
U.S. Patent Nos. 10,445,882, 10,662,013, 11,004,776 and 11,238,450 — all naming
Dr. James Wu as first inventor.

Procedural posture as of March 15, 2024:
  - Aurora's motion to dismiss was denied in part on January 8, 2024.
  - Claim construction (Markman) hearing is scheduled for August 2024.
  - No trial date has been set. Counsel estimates trial no earlier than Q3 2025.

Exposure assessment by outside counsel (Wilson Sonsini):
  - Probable exposure range: $3.5 million to $8.0 million.
  - Counsel assesses the probability of an injunction as low, on the basis that
    DataFlow does not practise the asserted patents and would face difficulty
    demonstrating irreparable harm.
  - A licensing settlement in the range of $4 million to $6 million is
    considered the most likely outcome.

Financial statement treatment: the Company has NOT recorded a loss accrual, on
the basis that no loss is both probable and reasonably estimable within the
meaning of ASC 450. The range is disclosed but not accrued. Buyer's accounting
advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

Legal fees of $2.8 million were incurred in FY2023 in connection with this
matter and are treated as a non-recurring add-back in the quality of earnings
report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

Section 3.15 — Litigation
Except as set forth in Schedule 3.15:
(a) There is no Action pending or, to the Company's Knowledge, threatened
    against the Company that would reasonably be expected to result in
    liability in excess of $2.0 million.
(b) The Company is not subject to any outstanding order, decree, or judgment.
(c) As of the date hereof, the Company is a defendant in the matter of
    DataFlow Systems Inc. v. Aurora Technologies Inc. (Case No. 2023-CV-04821,
    U.S. District Court, Northern District of California), alleging patent
    infringement related to certain data processing algorithms. The Company
    believes these claims are without merit and intends to vigorously defend.
    The Company's outside counsel has assessed the probable exposure at
    $3.5 million to $8.0 million.

SECTION 3: NOTES TO NORMALIZATION ADJUSTMENTS
Note 1 - Restructuring Charges ($4.5M, FY2023)
    Severance and facility exit costs associated with the closure of the Austin
    development center in Q3 FY2023. 32 employees were affected. Management
    represents this program is complete and no further charges are expected.
    We consider this adjustment appropriate and non-recurring.

Note 2 - Non-recurring Legal Fees ($2.8M, FY2023)
    External counsel fees relating to the DataFlow Systems patent litigation
    (Case No. 2023-CV-04821). We note that this matter remains unresolved and
    that future periods may incur comparable fees. Buyer should treat this
    add-back with caution: it is non-recurring only if the litigation concludes.
    We have flagged this as a QUALIFIED ADJUSTMENT.

Note 3 - SOC 2 Remediation ($1.6M, FY2023)
    One-time external consulting and tooling spend to remediate control gaps
    identified in the FY2022 SOC 2 Type II examination. The FY2023 examination
    was issued with no exceptions. Adjustment accepted.

Note 4 - Founder Compensation Above Market ($1.9M, both years)
    CEO Elena Marsh and CTO Dr. James Wu receive aggregate cash compensation
    approximately $1.9 million above the 75th percentile of the peer benchmark
    set. Post-closing employment terms are addressed in the retention agreements
    described in the employment agreement schedule. Adjustment accepted.

Note 5 - Capitalized Software Adjustment (($3.2M), FY2023)
    The Company capitalizes internally developed software over a 3-year life.
    Peer practice in this segment is predominantly to expense. We have reduced
    EBITDA by the amount capitalized in each period to present a comparable
    figure. This is a DOWNWARD adjustment and reduces Adjusted EBITDA.

Note 6 - Deferred Revenue Haircut Reversal (($1.4M), FY2023)
    Purchase accounting will require a fair value haircut to acquired deferred
    revenue, estimated at $1.4 million. This reduces post-closing recognized
    revenue and is presented here so the Buyer models the correct run-rate.

SPEAKER NOTES:
- CFO Sarah Chen noted that the $4.5M restructuring charge in FY2023 was
  related to the closure of the Austin development center (32 employees)
  and should be added back for Adjusted EBITDA calculation.
- Board member David Park raised concerns about customer concentration risk
  and requested management prepare a sensitivity analysis assuming loss of
  the top 3 customers.
- General Counsel Maria Rodriguez confirmed that the DataFlow litigation
  reserve of $5.0M is reflected in the FY2023 balance sheet under
  Accrued Liabilities.

SECTION 6: KEY OBSERVATIONS FOR THE BUYER
1. Adjusted EBITDA of $99.0 million exceeds reported EBITDA of $92.8 million by
   $6.2 million. A valuation struck on Adjusted EBITDA rather than reported
   EBITDA produces a materially lower implied multiple.

2. The DataFlow legal fee add-back ($2.8M) is qualified. If the litigation
   continues into FY2024, Adjusted EBITDA is overstated by that amount.

3. Perpetual license revenue is in structural decline and should be excluded
   from run-rate assumptions.

4. Founder compensation normalization assumes both founders remain. If either
   departs, replacement cost at market may exceed the $1.9 million add-back.

5. The capitalized software adjustment is the single largest downward
   normalization and reflects a genuine accounting policy difference, not an
   earnings quality concern.

Section 8.1(k) of the Credit Agreement defines an Event of Default to include
any transaction in which any person or group acquires beneficial ownership of
more than 35% of the voting equity of the Company.

The Vertex Capital Partners merger constitutes a change of control within this
definition. On the occurrence of such an Event of Default:

  - All outstanding principal, accrued interest and fees become immediately due
    and payable without further notice or demand.

Consequence for the transaction: the full $85 million drawn balance must be
repaid at closing. There is no prepayment penalty, but accrued interest and a
breakage indemnity for any SOFR period terminated mid-period will be payable.
Estimated breakage cost: less than $50,000.

The Company has NOT sought a consent or waiver from the lending syndicate.
Buyer's financing plan assumes the facility is repaid and replaced. The merger
agreement requires delivery of a customary payoff letter and lien releases at
closing as a condition to Buyer's obligation to close.

infringes U.S. Patent Nos. 9,847,221 and 10,112,905, both directed to methods

Dr. James Wu as first inventor.

Procedural posture as of March 15, 2024:

  - Claim construction (Markman) hearing is scheduled for August 2024.
  - No trial date has been set. Counsel estimates trial no earlier than Q3 2025.

  - Probable exposure range: $3.5 million to $8.0 million.
  - Counsel assesses the probability of an injunction as low, on the basis that

    demonstrating irreparable harm.

    considered the most likely outcome.

the basis that no loss is both probable and reasonably estimable within the
meaning of ASC 450. The range is disclosed but not accrued. Buyer's accounting
advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

matter and are treated as a non-recurring add-back in the quality of earnings
report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

No foreign investment or national security filing is required. Aurora holds no
government contracts, no facility security clearance, and no controlled
technology subject to ITAR or the EAR beyond mass-market encryption eligible for
License Exception ENC.

Business Associate Agreement dated April 12, 2022. Aurora's HIPAA compliance
programme was reviewed and no material gaps were identified. The BAA does not
contain an assignment restriction and survives a change of control.

SECTION 4: KEY PERSON DEPENDENCY
Dr. James Wu, Chief Technology Officer, is named as sole or first inventor on 12
of the Company's 47 issued U.S. patents, including the four patents underlying
the real-time data reconciliation engine that is the subject of the DataFlow
Systems litigation.

Dr. Wu's employment agreement contains:
  - A non-competition covenant of 12 months post-termination, enforceable in
    Delaware but of uncertain enforceability in California, where he resides.
  - A non-solicitation covenant of 24 months.
  - An assignment-of-inventions clause covering all work product.

Dr. Wu has NOT executed a post-closing employment agreement with Vertex Capital
Partners. Buyer has identified this as a material integration risk. Aurora
management represents that Dr. Wu has verbally indicated willingness to remain
for a transition period of not less than 12 months, but this is not documented.

therefore expected to be triggered.

SECTION 4: CHANGE OF CONTROL AND THE TRANSACTION
Section 8.1(k) of the Credit Agreement defines an Event of Default to include
any transaction in which any person or group acquires beneficial ownership of
more than 35% of the voting equity of the Company.

The Vertex Capital Partners merger constitutes a change of control within this
definition. On the occurrence of such an Event of Default:

  - All commitments terminate automatically;
  - All outstanding principal, accrued interest and fees become immediately due
    and payable without further notice or demand.

Consequence for the transaction: the full $85 million drawn balance must be
repaid at closing. There is no prepayment penalty, but accrued interest and a
breakage indemnity for any SOFR period terminated mid-period will be payable.
Estimated breakage cost: less than $50,000.

The Company has NOT sought a consent or waiver from the lending syndicate.
Buyer's financing plan assumes the facility is repaid and replaced. The merger
agreement requires delivery of a customary payoff letter and lien releases at
closing as a condition to Buyer's obligation to close.

DataFlow Systems Inc. alleges that Aurora's real-time data reconciliation engine
infringes U.S. Patent Nos. 9,847,221 and 10,112,905, both directed to methods
for incremental reconciliation of distributed record sets.

The four Aurora patents most closely related to the accused functionality are
U.S. Patent Nos. 10,445,882, 10,662,013, 11,004,776 and 11,238,450 — all naming
Dr. James Wu as first inventor.

Procedural posture as of March 15, 2024:
  - Aurora's motion to dismiss was denied in part on January 8, 2024.
  - Claim construction (Markman) hearing is scheduled for August 2024.
  - No trial date has been set. Counsel estimates trial no earlier than Q3 2025.

  - Probable exposure range: $3.5 million to $8.0 million.
  - Counsel assesses the probability of an injunction as low, on the basis that
    DataFlow does not practise the asserted patents and would face difficulty
    demonstrating irreparable harm.
  - A licensing settlement in the range of $4 million to $6 million is
    considered the most likely outcome.

the basis that no loss is both probable and reasonably estimable within the
meaning of ASC 450. The range is disclosed but not accrued. Buyer's accounting
advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

matter and are treated as a non-recurring add-back in the quality of earnings
report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

    Severance and facility exit costs associated with the closure of the Austin
    development center in Q3 FY2023. 32 employees were affected. Management
    represents this program is complete and no further charges are expected.
    We consider this adjustment appropriate and non-recurring.

Note 2 - Non-recurring Legal Fees ($2.8M, FY2023)
    External counsel fees relating to the DataFlow Systems patent litigation
    (Case No. 2023-CV-04821). We note that this matter remains unresolved and
    that future periods may incur comparable fees. Buyer should treat this
    add-back with caution: it is non-recurring only if the litigation concludes.
    We have flagged this as a QUALIFIED ADJUSTMENT.

Note 3 - SOC 2 Remediation ($1.6M, FY2023)
    One-time external consulting and tooling spend to remediate control gaps
    identified in the FY2022 SOC 2 Type II examination. The FY2023 examination
    was issued with no exceptions. Adjustment accepted.

Note 4 - Founder Compensation Above Market ($1.9M, both years)
    CEO Elena Marsh and CTO Dr. James Wu receive aggregate cash compensation
    approximately $1.9 million above the 75th percentile of the peer benchmark
    set. Post-closing employment terms are addressed in the retention agreements
    described in the employment agreement schedule. Adjustment accepted.

Note 5 - Capitalized Software Adjustment (($3.2M), FY2023)
    The Company capitalizes internally developed software over a 3-year life.
    Peer practice in this segment is predominantly to expense. We have reduced
    EBITDA by the amount capitalized in each period to present a comparable
    figure. This is a DOWNWARD adjustment and reduces Adjusted EBITDA.

    revenue, estimated at $1.4 million. This reduces post-closing recognized
    revenue and is presented here so the Buyer models the correct run-rate.

Dr. James Wu as first inventor.

  - Probable exposure range: $3.5 million to $8.0 million.
  - Counsel assesses the probability of an injunction as low, on the basis that
    DataFlow does not practise the asserted patents and would face difficulty
    demonstrating irreparable harm.
  - A licensing settlement in the range of $4 million to $6 million is
    considered the most likely outcome.

the basis that no loss is both probable and reasonably estimable within the
meaning of ASC 450. The range is disclosed but not accrued. Buyer's accounting
advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

matter and are treated as a non-recurring add-back in the quality of earnings
report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

query: The quality of earnings report adds back DataFlow legal fees. What is the litigation status and is that add-back safe?

reranked.text:
DataFlow Systems Inc. alleges that Aurora's real-time data reconciliation engine
infringes U.S. Patent Nos. 9,847,221 and 10,112,905, both directed to methods
for incremental reconciliation of distributed record sets.

The four Aurora patents most closely related to the accused functionality are
U.S. Patent Nos. 10,445,882, 10,662,013, 11,004,776 and 11,238,450 — all naming
Dr. James Wu as first inventor.

Procedural posture as of March 15, 2024:
  - Aurora's motion to dismiss was denied in part on January 8, 2024.
  - Claim construction (Markman) hearing is scheduled for August 2024.
  - No trial date has been set. Counsel estimates trial no earlier than Q3 2025.

Exposure assessment by outside counsel (Wilson Sonsini):
  - Probable exposure range: $3.5 million to $8.0 million.
  - Counsel assesses the probability of an injunction as low, on the basis that
    DataFlow does not practise the asserted patents and would face difficulty
    demonstrating irreparable harm.
  - A licensing settlement in the range of $4 million to $6 million is
    considered the most likely outcome.

Financial statement treatment: the Company has NOT recorded a loss accrual, on
the basis that no loss is both probable and reasonably estimable within the
meaning of ASC 450. The range is disclosed but not accrued. Buyer's accounting
advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

Legal fees of $2.8 million were incurred in FY2023 in connection with this
matter and are treated as a non-recurring add-back in the quality of earnings
report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

SECTION 6: KEY OBSERVATIONS FOR THE BUYER
1. Adjusted EBITDA of $99.0 million exceeds reported EBITDA of $92.8 million by
   $6.2 million. A valuation struck on Adjusted EBITDA rather than reported
   EBITDA produces a materially lower implied multiple.

2. The DataFlow legal fee add-back ($2.8M) is qualified. If the litigation
   continues into FY2024, Adjusted EBITDA is overstated by that amount.

3. Perpetual license revenue is in structural decline and should be excluded
   from run-rate assumptions.

4. Founder compensation normalization assumes both founders remain. If either
   departs, replacement cost at market may exceed the $1.9 million add-back.

5. The capitalized software adjustment is the single largest downward
   normalization and reflects a genuine accounting policy difference, not an
   earnings quality concern.

DataFlow Systems Inc. alleges that Aurora's real-time data reconciliation engine
infringes U.S. Patent Nos. 9,847,221 and 10,112,905, both directed to methods
for incremental reconciliation of distributed record sets.

The four Aurora patents most closely related to the accused functionality are
U.S. Patent Nos. 10,445,882, 10,662,013, 11,004,776 and 11,238,450 — all naming
Dr. James Wu as first inventor.

Procedural posture as of March 15, 2024:
  - Aurora's motion to dismiss was denied in part on January 8, 2024.
  - Claim construction (Markman) hearing is scheduled for August 2024.
  - No trial date has been set. Counsel estimates trial no earlier than Q3 2025.

Exposure assessment by outside counsel (Wilson Sonsini):
  - Probable exposure range: $3.5 million to $8.0 million.
  - Counsel assesses the probability of an injunction as low, on the basis that
    DataFlow does not practise the asserted patents and would face difficulty
    demonstrating irreparable harm.
  - A licensing settlement in the range of $4 million to $6 million is
    considered the most likely outcome.

Financial statement treatment: the Company has NOT recorded a loss accrual, on
the basis that no loss is both probable and reasonably estimable within the
meaning of ASC 450. The range is disclosed but not accrued. Buyer's accounting
advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

SECTION 4: CONDITIONS TO CLOSING
The regulatory conditions to closing under Article VI of the merger agreement
are:

  1. Expiration or early termination of the HSR waiting period.
  2. No injunction or order prohibiting the transaction.
  3. No law enacted after signing that makes the transaction illegal.

There is no financing condition. There is no condition relating to obtaining
customer consents, notwithstanding that two material customer contracts
(Northstar Financial Group and Pacific Data Systems, together representing
$92.8 million or 20.5% of FY2023 revenue) contain consent-based termination
rights. Buyer therefore bears the risk of those consents not being obtained.

Counsel draws attention to this allocation: the customer consent risk sits with
the Buyer post-closing rather than operating as a condition, and is addressed,
if at all, through the indemnification provisions in Article VIII.

SECTION 4: CHANGE OF CONTROL AND THE TRANSACTION
Section 8.1(k) of the Credit Agreement defines an Event of Default to include
any transaction in which any person or group acquires beneficial ownership of
more than 35% of the voting equity of the Company.

The Vertex Capital Partners merger constitutes a change of control within this
definition. On the occurrence of such an Event of Default:

  - All commitments terminate automatically;
  - All outstanding principal, accrued interest and fees become immediately due
    and payable without further notice or demand.

Consequence for the transaction: the full $85 million drawn balance must be
repaid at closing. There is no prepayment penalty, but accrued interest and a
breakage indemnity for any SOFR period terminated mid-period will be payable.
Estimated breakage cost: less than $50,000.

The Company has NOT sought a consent or waiver from the lending syndicate.
Buyer's financing plan assumes the facility is repaid and replaced. The merger
agreement requires delivery of a customary payoff letter and lien releases at
closing as a condition to Buyer's obligation to close.

DataFlow Systems Inc. alleges that Aurora's real-time data reconciliation engine
infringes U.S. Patent Nos. 9,847,221 and 10,112,905, both directed to methods
for incremental reconciliation of distributed record sets.

The four Aurora patents most closely related to the accused functionality are
U.S. Patent Nos. 10,445,882, 10,662,013, 11,004,776 and 11,238,450 — all naming
Dr. James Wu as first inventor.

Procedural posture as of March 15, 2024:
  - Aurora's motion to dismiss was denied in part on January 8, 2024.
  - Claim construction (Markman) hearing is scheduled for August 2024.
  - No trial date has been set. Counsel estimates trial no earlier than Q3 2025.

Exposure assessment by outside counsel (Wilson Sonsini):
  - Probable exposure range: $3.5 million to $8.0 million.
  - Counsel assesses the probability of an injunction as low, on the basis that
    DataFlow does not practise the asserted patents and would face difficulty
    demonstrating irreparable harm.
  - A licensing settlement in the range of $4 million to $6 million is
    considered the most likely outcome.

Financial statement treatment: the Company has NOT recorded a loss accrual, on
the basis that no loss is both probable and reasonably estimable within the
meaning of ASC 450. The range is disclosed but not accrued. Buyer's accounting
advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

Legal fees of $2.8 million were incurred in FY2023 in connection with this
matter and are treated as a non-recurring add-back in the quality of earnings
report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

of accrual completeness, examination of non-recurring items, and normalization
of reported EBITDA.

by Deloitte & Touche LLP, which issued an unqualified opinion for both periods.

SECTION 4: CHANGE OF CONTROL AND THE TRANSACTION
Section 8.1(k) of the Credit Agreement defines an Event of Default to include
any transaction in which any person or group acquires beneficial ownership of
more than 35% of the voting equity of the Company.

The Vertex Capital Partners merger constitutes a change of control within this
definition. On the occurrence of such an Event of Default:

  - All commitments terminate automatically;
  - All outstanding principal, accrued interest and fees become immediately due
    and payable without further notice or demand.

Consequence for the transaction: the full $85 million drawn balance must be
repaid at closing. There is no prepayment penalty, but accrued interest and a
breakage indemnity for any SOFR period terminated mid-period will be payable.
Estimated breakage cost: less than $50,000.

The Company has NOT sought a consent or waiver from the lending syndicate.
Buyer's financing plan assumes the facility is repaid and replaced. The merger
agreement requires delivery of a customary payoff letter and lien releases at
closing as a condition to Buyer's obligation to close.

Note 1 - Restructuring Charges ($4.5M, FY2023)
    Severance and facility exit costs associated with the closure of the Austin
    development center in Q3 FY2023. 32 employees were affected. Management
    represents this program is complete and no further charges are expected.
    We consider this adjustment appropriate and non-recurring.

Note 2 - Non-recurring Legal Fees ($2.8M, FY2023)
    External counsel fees relating to the DataFlow Systems patent litigation
    (Case No. 2023-CV-04821). We note that this matter remains unresolved and
    that future periods may incur comparable fees. Buyer should treat this
    add-back with caution: it is non-recurring only if the litigation concludes.
    We have flagged this as a QUALIFIED ADJUSTMENT.

Note 3 - SOC 2 Remediation ($1.6M, FY2023)
    One-time external consulting and tooling spend to remediate control gaps
    identified in the FY2022 SOC 2 Type II examination. The FY2023 examination
    was issued with no exceptions. Adjustment accepted.

Note 4 - Founder Compensation Above Market ($1.9M, both years)
    CEO Elena Marsh and CTO Dr. James Wu receive aggregate cash compensation
    approximately $1.9 million above the 75th percentile of the peer benchmark
    set. Post-closing employment terms are addressed in the retention agreements
    described in the employment agreement schedule. Adjustment accepted.

Note 5 - Capitalized Software Adjustment (($3.2M), FY2023)
    The Company capitalizes internally developed software over a 3-year life.
    Peer practice in this segment is predominantly to expense. We have reduced
    EBITDA by the amount capitalized in each period to present a comparable
    figure. This is a DOWNWARD adjustment and reduces Adjusted EBITDA.

Note 6 - Deferred Revenue Haircut Reversal (($1.4M), FY2023)
    Purchase accounting will require a fair value haircut to acquired deferred
    revenue, estimated at $1.4 million. This reduces post-closing recognized
    revenue and is presented here so the Buyer models the correct run-rate.

attributable to a single incident in August 2023 affecting the Meridian Health

confirm the BAA survives the transaction.

three master lease schedules maturing between 2025 and 2027. Two of the three

lessor in each case is the same counterparty and has indicated in writing that
consent will be granted upon customary notice.

remaining terms, principally the San Jose headquarters lease expiring in 2029.

    DataFlow does not practise the asserted patents and would face difficulty
    demonstrating irreparable harm.

    considered the most likely outcome.

advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

matter and are treated as a non-recurring add-back in the quality of earnings
report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

infringes U.S. Patent Nos. 9,847,221 and 10,112,905, both directed to methods
for incremental reconciliation of distributed record sets.

U.S. Patent Nos. 10,445,882, 10,662,013, 11,004,776 and 11,238,450 — all naming
Dr. James Wu as first inventor.

Procedural posture as of March 15, 2024:
  - Aurora's motion to dismiss was denied in part on January 8, 2024.
  - Claim construction (Markman) hearing is scheduled for August 2024.
  - No trial date has been set. Counsel estimates trial no earlier than Q3 2025.

Exposure assessment by outside counsel (Wilson Sonsini):
  - Probable exposure range: $3.5 million to $8.0 million.
  - Counsel assesses the probability of an injunction as low, on the basis that
    DataFlow does not practise the asserted patents and would face difficulty
    demonstrating irreparable harm.
  - A licensing settlement in the range of $4 million to $6 million is
    considered the most likely outcome.

Financial statement treatment: the Company has NOT recorded a loss accrual, on
the basis that no loss is both probable and reasonably estimable within the
meaning of ASC 450. The range is disclosed but not accrued. Buyer's accounting
advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

Legal fees of $2.8 million were incurred in FY2023 in connection with this
matter and are treated as a non-recurring add-back in the quality of earnings
report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

SECTION 4: KEY PERSON DEPENDENCY
Dr. James Wu, Chief Technology Officer, is named as sole or first inventor on 12
of the Company's 47 issued U.S. patents, including the four patents underlying
the real-time data reconciliation engine that is the subject of the DataFlow
Systems litigation.

Dr. Wu's employment agreement contains:
  - A non-competition covenant of 12 months post-termination, enforceable in
    Delaware but of uncertain enforceability in California, where he resides.
  - A non-solicitation covenant of 24 months.
  - An assignment-of-inventions clause covering all work product.

Dr. Wu has NOT executed a post-closing employment agreement with Vertex Capital
Partners. Buyer has identified this as a material integration risk. Aurora
management represents that Dr. Wu has verbally indicated willingness to remain
for a transition period of not less than 12 months, but this is not documented.

CEO Elena Marsh has indicated she intends to depart at closing. Her severance is
therefore expected to be triggered.

SECTION 3: NOTES TO NORMALIZATION ADJUSTMENTS
Note 1 - Restructuring Charges ($4.5M, FY2023)
    Severance and facility exit costs associated with the closure of the Austin
    development center in Q3 FY2023. 32 employees were affected. Management
    represents this program is complete and no further charges are expected.
    We consider this adjustment appropriate and non-recurring.

Note 2 - Non-recurring Legal Fees ($2.8M, FY2023)
    External counsel fees relating to the DataFlow Systems patent litigation
    (Case No. 2023-CV-04821). We note that this matter remains unresolved and
    that future periods may incur comparable fees. Buyer should treat this
    add-back with caution: it is non-recurring only if the litigation concludes.
    We have flagged this as a QUALIFIED ADJUSTMENT.

Note 3 - SOC 2 Remediation ($1.6M, FY2023)
    One-time external consulting and tooling spend to remediate control gaps
    identified in the FY2022 SOC 2 Type II examination. The FY2023 examination
    was issued with no exceptions. Adjustment accepted.

Note 4 - Founder Compensation Above Market ($1.9M, both years)
    CEO Elena Marsh and CTO Dr. James Wu receive aggregate cash compensation
    approximately $1.9 million above the 75th percentile of the peer benchmark
    set. Post-closing employment terms are addressed in the retention agreements
    described in the employment agreement schedule. Adjustment accepted.

Note 5 - Capitalized Software Adjustment (($3.2M), FY2023)
    The Company capitalizes internally developed software over a 3-year life.
    Peer practice in this segment is predominantly to expense. We have reduced
    EBITDA by the amount capitalized in each period to present a comparable
    figure. This is a DOWNWARD adjustment and reduces Adjusted EBITDA.

Note 6 - Deferred Revenue Haircut Reversal (($1.4M), FY2023)
    Purchase accounting will require a fair value haircut to acquired deferred
    revenue, estimated at $1.4 million. This reduces post-closing recognized
    revenue and is presented here so the Buyer models the correct run-rate.

advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

    add-back with caution: it is non-recurring only if the litigation concludes.

    demonstrating irreparable harm.

Systems litigation.

Dr. Wu's employment agreement contains:

    Delaware but of uncertain enforceability in California, where he resides.
  - A non-solicitation covenant of 24 months.

Dr. Wu has NOT executed a post-closing employment agreement with Vertex Capital
Partners. Buyer has identified this as a material integration risk. Aurora
management represents that Dr. Wu has verbally indicated willingness to remain
for a transition period of not less than 12 months, but this is not documented.

CEO Elena Marsh has indicated she intends to depart at closing. Her severance is
therefore expected to be triggered.

SECTION 4: CHANGE OF CONTROL AND THE TRANSACTION
Section 8.1(k) of the Credit Agreement defines an Event of Default to include
any transaction in which any person or group acquires beneficial ownership of
more than 35% of the voting equity of the Company.

The Vertex Capital Partners merger constitutes a change of control within this
definition. On the occurrence of such an Event of Default:

  - All commitments terminate automatically;
  - All outstanding principal, accrued interest and fees become immediately due
    and payable without further notice or demand.

Consequence for the transaction: the full $85 million drawn balance must be
repaid at closing. There is no prepayment penalty, but accrued interest and a
breakage indemnity for any SOFR period terminated mid-period will be payable.
Estimated breakage cost: less than $50,000.

The Company has NOT sought a consent or waiver from the lending syndicate.
Buyer's financing plan assumes the facility is repaid and replaced. The merger
agreement requires delivery of a customary payoff letter and lien releases at
closing as a condition to Buyer's obligation to close.

SECTION 4: CHANGE OF CONTROL AND THE TRANSACTION
Section 8.1(k) of the Credit Agreement defines an Event of Default to include
any transaction in which any person or group acquires beneficial ownership of
more than 35% of the voting equity of the Company.

The Vertex Capital Partners merger constitutes a change of control within this
definition. On the occurrence of such an Event of Default:

  - All commitments terminate automatically;
  - All outstanding principal, accrued interest and fees become immediately due
    and payable without further notice or demand.

Consequence for the transaction: the full $85 million drawn balance must be
repaid at closing. There is no prepayment penalty, but accrued interest and a
breakage indemnity for any SOFR period terminated mid-period will be payable.
Estimated breakage cost: less than $50,000.

The Company has NOT sought a consent or waiver from the lending syndicate.
Buyer's financing plan assumes the facility is repaid and replaced. The merger
agreement requires delivery of a customary payoff letter and lien releases at
closing as a condition to Buyer's obligation to close.

SECTION 1: ANTITRUST AND MERGER CONTROL
HART-SCOTT-RODINO (UNITED STATES)
The transaction is reportable under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements
Act. The transaction value of approximately $696 million exceeds the size-of-
transaction threshold, and both parties exceed the size-of-person thresholds.

SECTION 4: CONDITIONS TO CLOSING
The regulatory conditions to closing under Article VI of the merger agreement
are:

  1. Expiration or early termination of the HSR waiting period.
  2. No injunction or order prohibiting the transaction.
  3. No law enacted after signing that makes the transaction illegal.

There is no financing condition. There is no condition relating to obtaining
customer consents, notwithstanding that two material customer contracts
(Northstar Financial Group and Pacific Data Systems, together representing
$92.8 million or 20.5% of FY2023 revenue) contain consent-based termination
rights. Buyer therefore bears the risk of those consents not being obtained.

Counsel draws attention to this allocation: the customer consent risk sits with
the Buyer post-closing rather than operating as a condition, and is addressed,
if at all, through the indemnification provisions in Article VIII.

SECTION 5: SERVICE LEVEL COMMITMENTS AND PENALTIES
Northstar Financial Group and Meridian Health Networks contracts include
uptime service level agreements of 99.95% measured monthly, with service
credits of up to 15% of monthly fees for sustained breach.

During FY2023 the Company recorded $0.6 million in service credits, all
attributable to a single incident in August 2023 affecting the Meridian Health
Networks environment. No customer exercised a termination right as a result.

Meridian Health Networks is subject to HIPAA. The Company executed a Business
Associate Agreement dated April 12, 2022. Buyer's regulatory counsel should
confirm the BAA survives the transaction.

SECURITY INCIDENTS
One security incident occurred during the review period. In August 2023 a
misconfigured storage bucket in a non-production environment was accessible
without authentication for approximately 41 hours. The environment contained
synthetic test data only. No personal data or customer data was exposed. Counsel
confirmed no notification obligation arose under GDPR, CCPA or any state breach
notification statute. The incident is unrelated to the service credit recorded
for the Meridian Health Networks availability event in the same month.

SECTION 3: NOTES TO NORMALIZATION ADJUSTMENTS
Note 1 - Restructuring Charges ($4.5M, FY2023)
    Severance and facility exit costs associated with the closure of the Austin
    development center in Q3 FY2023. 32 employees were affected. Management
    represents this program is complete and no further charges are expected.
    We consider this adjustment appropriate and non-recurring.

Note 2 - Non-recurring Legal Fees ($2.8M, FY2023)
    External counsel fees relating to the DataFlow Systems patent litigation
    (Case No. 2023-CV-04821). We note that this matter remains unresolved and
    that future periods may incur comparable fees. Buyer should treat this
    add-back with caution: it is non-recurring only if the litigation concludes.
    We have flagged this as a QUALIFIED ADJUSTMENT.

Note 3 - SOC 2 Remediation ($1.6M, FY2023)
    One-time external consulting and tooling spend to remediate control gaps
    identified in the FY2022 SOC 2 Type II examination. The FY2023 examination
    was issued with no exceptions. Adjustment accepted.

Note 4 - Founder Compensation Above Market ($1.9M, both years)
    CEO Elena Marsh and CTO Dr. James Wu receive aggregate cash compensation
    approximately $1.9 million above the 75th percentile of the peer benchmark
    set. Post-closing employment terms are addressed in the retention agreements
    described in the employment agreement schedule. Adjustment accepted.

Note 5 - Capitalized Software Adjustment (($3.2M), FY2023)
    The Company capitalizes internally developed software over a 3-year life.
    Peer practice in this segment is predominantly to expense. We have reduced
    EBITDA by the amount capitalized in each period to present a comparable
    figure. This is a DOWNWARD adjustment and reduces Adjusted EBITDA.

Note 6 - Deferred Revenue Haircut Reversal (($1.4M), FY2023)
    Purchase accounting will require a fair value haircut to acquired deferred
    revenue, estimated at $1.4 million. This reduces post-closing recognized
    revenue and is presented here so the Buyer models the correct run-rate.

Dr. James Wu, Chief Technology Officer, is named as sole or first inventor on 12
of the Company's 47 issued U.S. patents, including the four patents underlying
the real-time data reconciliation engine that is the subject of the DataFlow
Systems litigation.

Dr. Wu's employment agreement contains:
  - A non-competition covenant of 12 months post-termination, enforceable in
    Delaware but of uncertain enforceability in California, where he resides.
  - A non-solicitation covenant of 24 months.
  - An assignment-of-inventions clause covering all work product.

Dr. Wu has NOT executed a post-closing employment agreement with Vertex Capital
Partners. Buyer has identified this as a material integration risk. Aurora
management represents that Dr. Wu has verbally indicated willingness to remain
for a transition period of not less than 12 months, but this is not documented.

CEO Elena Marsh has indicated she intends to depart at closing. Her severance is
therefore expected to be triggered.

SECTION 4: KEY PERSON DEPENDENCY
Dr. James Wu, Chief Technology Officer, is named as sole or first inventor on 12
of the Company's 47 issued U.S. patents, including the four patents underlying
the real-time data reconciliation engine that is the subject of the DataFlow
Systems litigation.

Dr. Wu's employment agreement contains:
  - A non-competition covenant of 12 months post-termination, enforceable in
    Delaware but of uncertain enforceability in California, where he resides.
  - A non-solicitation covenant of 24 months.
  - An assignment-of-inventions clause covering all work product.

Dr. Wu has NOT executed a post-closing employment agreement with Vertex Capital
Partners. Buyer has identified this as a material integration risk. Aurora
management represents that Dr. Wu has verbally indicated willingness to remain
for a transition period of not less than 12 months, but this is not documented.

CEO Elena Marsh has indicated she intends to depart at closing. Her severance is
therefore expected to be triggered.

DataFlow Systems Inc. alleges that Aurora's real-time data reconciliation engine
infringes U.S. Patent Nos. 9,847,221 and 10,112,905, both directed to methods
for incremental reconciliation of distributed record sets.

The four Aurora patents most closely related to the accused functionality are
U.S. Patent Nos. 10,445,882, 10,662,013, 11,004,776 and 11,238,450 — all naming
Dr. James Wu as first inventor.

Procedural posture as of March 15, 2024:
  - Aurora's motion to dismiss was denied in part on January 8, 2024.
  - Claim construction (Markman) hearing is scheduled for August 2024.
  - No trial date has been set. Counsel estimates trial no earlier than Q3 2025.

Exposure assessment by outside counsel (Wilson Sonsini):
  - Probable exposure range: $3.5 million to $8.0 million.
  - Counsel assesses the probability of an injunction as low, on the basis that
    DataFlow does not practise the asserted patents and would face difficulty
    demonstrating irreparable harm.
  - A licensing settlement in the range of $4 million to $6 million is
    considered the most likely outcome.

Financial statement treatment: the Company has NOT recorded a loss accrual, on
the basis that no loss is both probable and reasonably estimable within the
meaning of ASC 450. The range is disclosed but not accrued. Buyer's accounting
advisers have flagged this as an area of judgement.

Legal fees of $2.8 million were incurred in FY2023 in connection with this
matter and are treated as a non-recurring add-back in the quality of earnings
report. That add-back is qualified: the litigation is unresolved and comparable
fees are likely in FY2024.

SLIDE 2: MARKET CONTEXT
Industry Trends:
- Enterprise software M&A activity up 34% YoY in 2023
- Median EV/Revenue multiple for SaaS companies: 8.2x (down from 12.4x in 2021)
- Median EV/EBITDA multiple for profitable SaaS: 22.5x
- Private equity dry powder at record $2.6 trillion

Aurora's Position:
- #3 market share in enterprise data analytics (est. 8.2% market share)
- Market leader: Palantir (18.4%), #2: Snowflake (12.1%)
- Strong customer retention: 118% Net Revenue Retention
- Accelerating SaaS transition: SaaS mix grew from 38.3% to 41.9% of revenue

Competitive Risks:
- AI-native competitors gaining traction (Databricks, DataRobot)
- Customer concentration: Top 10 customers represent 28% of revenue
- Key person dependency: CTO Dr. James Wu holds 12 critical patents

There is no other pending or, to the Company's knowledge, threatened litigation
against the Company other than the following:

     approximately EUR 310,000 of disputed commissions. No proceedings have been
     commenced. The Company has accrued EUR 180,000.

No governmental investigation, subpoena, or civil investigative demand is
